name: Wang Jingwei
role: Chinese Nationalist politician and head of the Japanese-backed Nanjing government (1940–1944)
summary: Wang’s republican nationalism developed into a program of accommodation with Japan, militant anti-communism and an East Asian bloc against Western powers. His constitutional promises conflicted with collaborationist repression, propaganda control and a leadership cult; his later rhetoric also included antisemitic conspiracy claims.

public-ownership.rationale: He explicitly endorses government ownership of large public utilities in his quoted economic program.

unions-good.rationale: In 1924 he said the party gave great weight to organising workers and farmers and to their rightful claims.

regulate-corporations.rationale: His economic program demands legal restrictions on monopolistic private ownership.

worker-ownership.rationale: In 1927 he described worker-managed factories as unsustainable and a communist device, though he did not rule out state management.

strong-leader.rationale: He demanded Chiang Kai-shek's resignation in 1931 to end personal dictatorship and called personal dictatorship a cause of national ruin in 1940.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: His educational program emphasizes Chinese cultural nationalism and national legitimacy.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: In 1919 he called the League of Nations the germ of human coexistence and said China should help it grow.

revolution-justified.rationale: His revolutionary record and later self-presentation affirm the legitimacy of overthrowing Qing rule.

state-directs-investment.rationale: His treaty provides state-coordinated strategic resource development and industrial rehabilitation.

one-party-rule.rationale: His reorganized Nationalist party directs the regime’s political and ideological apparatus.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He attempts to overthrow Qing dynastic rule and continues to advocate republican constitutional government.

democracy-best.rationale: His constitutional promises conflict with authoritarian rule and organized repression.

direct-votes.rationale: He stated that the party's democracy principle includes the exercise of direct people's rights alongside the five-power constitution.

right-to-secede.rationale: In 1938 he said only national unity and no regional separatism was acceptable; in 1944 he told his followers that the party must be united and the nation indivisible.

political-violence-never.rationale: He attempts political assassination and later embraces armed anti-communist suppression.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Quoting Sun Yat-sen, he said society advances through the harmony of most economic interests, not their conflict, and rejected class struggle as the communists' creed.

civilizational-union.rationale: He advocates an East Asian political and military sphere founded on Sino-Japanese cooperation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: In 1927 he called the communists' proletarian dictatorship a deceit and said China needed a union of oppressed classes rather than rule by one class.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: In 1927 he said capitalism and imperialism are the same thing and that capitalist states use machine-guns against resistance, though he did not state a general law of war between powers.

conscription.rationale: In 1937 he treated conscription as part of 'those with strength contribute strength' and called for fixing its faults rather than dropping it.

national-rebirth.rationale: His own slogan was 'revive China and protect East Asia', which he tied to the Tongmenghui's 'restore China', and he repeated the call for national rebirth from 1938 to 1944.

class-collaboration.rationale: After the 1927 split he rejected class struggle as a method and said the various social forces must combine, with employers and workers kept in good relations; in 1938 he again called for harmony between labour and capital.

dominated-front.rationale: He supports a common Asian front against British, American and Dutch colonial domination.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: In 1913 he rested his humanitarianism on love, equality and liberty and said those who want equality with their superiors must grant it to those beneath them; later regime practice is not shown here.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He invokes the people’s wish for peace while heading a regime sustained by foreign occupation.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: In 1938 he said all organisations and propaganda contrary to the Three Principles would be actively suppressed, and in 1937 he said political association could be limited during the revolution.

separated-powers.rationale: He cited the five-power constitution as part of the party's Principle of Democracy, which he affirmed.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He framed the Minsheng programme as securing food, clothing, housing and transport for the poor majority by restraining capital and equalising land rights.

party-controls-media.rationale: Only a Wikipedia summary was cited; no source of the person's own words or record was reached.

party-commands-army.rationale: He held that the party should govern the army and said ignoring party discipline would turn this into 'army governs party', criticising 'party army' ideas that put the soldiers over the party.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: In 1927 he insisted on party organisation and discipline over the objections of those who wanted party rule by revolutionary methods, and said without discipline 'party governs state and army' collapses.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He commits to continuing military cooperation with Japan against communism.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: His government accepts Manchukuo’s separate status in its settlement with Japan.

leader-cult.rationale: He heads a mobilization movement that joins political instruction to adulation of his leadership.

land-redistribution.rationale: He explicitly rules out confiscation in implementing his economic program.

ban-cartels.rationale: Only a Wikipedia summary was cited; no source of the person's own words or record was reached.

patriotic-education.rationale: His government uses schooling to promote Chinese nationalism and political mobilization.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: His 1940 declaration welcomes foreign capital and technology to reconstruct China.

return-lost-territory.rationale: In 1937 he said resistance could gradually recover lost territory, while in 1938-44 he accepted peace with Japan without recovering the Northeast.

military-guardian-role.rationale: He denounced army-over-party rule and in 1944 said soldiers must not hold troops for themselves.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: His 1943 declaration depicts Jews as partners in an Anglo-American conspiracy of world control.

defeat-communism.rationale: His treaty commits to eliminating communist organizations, superseding his earlier communist alliance.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: In 1927 he said China would build a non-capitalist state but not a copy of Soviet Russia, and he later rejected both communism and Anglo-American individualism.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He commits the government to eliminating communist elements and organizations.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He embraces a Japanese-led military alignment rather than neutrality.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He wrote that economic power held by a few is as unjust and, in its harms, worse than political despotism, and attacked the view that capitalists must first be protected.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: His treaty explicitly permits Japanese military and naval stations within China.

open-diplomacy.rationale: He negotiated secret agreements governing foreign troops, transport and advisers.

women-suffrage.rationale: In 1919 he presented women's suffrage as a rising reform, describing its opponents as obstinate or frivolous.

national-resource-control.rationale: He asserts Chinese independence but grants Japan privileged access to strategic mineral resources.

notes:
No inferred answers. Reviewed the entire statement list and remaining nulls across themes. Later collaborationist commitments supersede his earlier anti-Japanese and pro-communist positions. Constitutional rhetoric and authoritarian practice are recorded as mixed evidence. His antisemitic conspiracy statements are not evidence of specific Nazi hereditary-race doctrine. No ecological or technological positions are inferred from modernization rhetoric. Treaty text and scholarly full works were downloaded and searched; the full 1940 declaration was read online when direct downloading was blocked. Foreign resource access is not treated as evidence about foreign purchases of strategic firms. His 1927 no-confiscation economic statement is retained where no later personal reversal was found.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 23 answers taken from it, 21 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Second, independent pass. Built from his own speeches and writings on Chinese Wikisource (1905 Minbao articles, 1912-13 letters and articles, 1919 essay, 1926-27 speeches, 1937-38 wartime broadcasts, the 1938 Yan telegram, the 1940 Peace Declaration, 1940-43 Nanjing speeches, the 1944 last testament), the 1940 treaty text, and one scholarly article; texts saved in scratchpad/sources/wang-jingwei/. Searched by theme: economy, land, labour, government and constitution, party and army, liberty, culture and Confucianism, religion, women, world order, alliances, treaties and bases, anti-communism, violence. Later positions supersede earlier (Wuhan-era sympathy for workers and farmers gives way to class collaboration after 1927; wartime resistance gives way to peace with Japan in 1938). No answer rests on what a Japanese or occupation authority did without his own statement or signature. The 1944 testament is cited with its authenticity unchecked and only for answers also supported elsewhere or at medium confidence. Britannica was blocked by a bot wall. Statements on press control, leader cult, antisemitic claims and the 1940 Manchukuo recognition were left null because no opened source of his own settles them.
